**Requirements** You're wielding a ranged weapon or a thrown weapon.

---

You let loose a projectile that flies true and leaves the blazing trail of a meteor behind it. Make a ranged Strike, ignoring the target's concealment and reducing the target's cover by one degree for only this Strike (greater to standard, standard to lesser, and lesser to none). If the Strike hits, the meteor trail hangs in the air. This gives the benefits of concealment negation and cover reduction to any attacks made against the creature (by anyone) until the start of your next turn.

**Requirements** You're wielding a staff.

---

You spin your staff with an impossibly quick twirling flourish, attacking two foes and transforming the momentum into magical energy to charge for your next Spellstrike. Make a melee Strike with your staff against one foe and then a second melee Strike with your staff against a different foe. Your multiple attack penalty applies to both of these attacks as normal.
backfillRows.why: AoN spell-2884 prints "Requirements You're wielding a staff." and "You spin your staff with an impossibly quick twirling flourish"; ours had no Requirements line and the legacy spell-1043 "with a twirling flourish".

findings.note: Inline Requirements line (sky-laughs-at-waves shape) plus the remaster body; the shipped descRefs (Spellstrike/actions) still matches the prose and is left untouched.

backfillRows.value:
**Requirements** You're wielding a melee weapon in two hands.

---

You swing your massive weapon, creating a wave of sonic vibrations that topples creatures. Make a melee Strike with your two-handed weapon. Each creature in a 15-foot cone from you must attempt a basic Fortitude save against your spell DC or take 2 sonic damage. On a critical failure, the creature is knocked prone. The target of your Strike must be within the cone or the effect fails.

---

**Heightened (+1)** The damage increases by 1.
backfillRows.why: AoN spell-2885 prints "Requirements You're wielding a melee weapon in two hands."; ours began at the body. The body and Heightened entry are the shipped text unchanged.

findings.note: Inline Requirements prefix only. The prefix carries no digit, so injectDamageArrow's first standalone "2" is still the damage number (see thunderous-strike#heightened-damage). descRefs (prone/conditions) untouched.

backfillRows.why: AoN spell-2885 prints "take 2 sonic damage" with "Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1."; without baseDamage, scaleDamage (src/rules/heightening.ts) returns null and the auto-heightened focus spell always shows 2.
AoN spell-2885: the 2 sonic damage hurts ("take 2 sonic damage"); every spell carrying baseDamage also carries damageKind.

findings.note: Two separate top-level fields, one row each. addDice("2","1",n) handles a flat base (rank 3 -> "4"). The existing heightening {interval:1,damageIncr:"1"} is already right and is not re-emitted.

backfillRows.value:
**Requirements** You're wielding an improvised weapon.

---

You cause the sheath of water and the improvised weapon it surrounds to surge outward with stupendous force as you attack. Make a melee Strike with your improvised weapon. The weapon then breaks, and each creature adjacent to you must succeed at a Fortitude saving throw against your spell DC or be pushed 5 feet away from you (10 feet on a critical failure). You can Stride after the target of your Strike if they are pushed but you must move the same distance and in the same direction.

If the item has a Hardness greater than your level, or if it's an artifact, cursed item, or other item that's difficult to break or destroy, it doesn't break and adjacent creatures don't need to attempt Fortitude saves.
backfillRows.why: AoN spell-2311 (Rival Academies pg. 82) prints "Requirements You're wielding an improvised weapon."; ours began at the body, which is kept unchanged.

findings.note: Inline Requirements prefix on the sky-laughs-at-waves shape. The finding's alternative (a Spell.requirements field + SpellDetail row + importer fill for all 44 spells) needs src/ and scripts/ edits outside this chunk: see CROSS-FILE GAPS.
